blueprint_concepts: Binomial sums by the integration technique (sum of C_r/(r+1))
Evaluation via the antiderivative; handling discontinuous antiderivatives
english: For a real number $t$, let $\{t\}$ denote the fractional part of $t$. Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{9}\binom{9}{r}(-2)^{9-r}\{x\}^{r}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{10}f(x)\,dx$ is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $t$ के लिए माना $\{t\}$, $t$ का भिन्नात्मक भाग दर्शाता है। माना $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{9}\binom{9}{r}(-2)^{9-r}\{x\}^{r}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{10}f(x)\,dx$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $F(x)=\dfrac{(\{x\}-2)^{10}}{10}$ satisfies $F'=f$ on each $(k,k+1)$ but jumps at every integer, so $F(10)-F(0)=0$ is not the integral
solution_full: By the binomial theorem, $\sum_{r=0}^{9}\binom{9}{r}\{x\}^{r}(-2)^{9-r}=\left(\{x\}-2\right)^{9}$, so $f(x)=(\{x\}-2)^{9}$. Since $\{x+1\}=\{x\}$, $f$ has period $1$.

A tempting antiderivative is $F(x)=\dfrac{(\{x\}-2)^{10}}{10}$: on each open interval $(k,k+1)$, $\{x\}=x-k$ and $F'(x)=f(x)$. But $F$ is not continuous at the integers ($F(k^{-})=\dfrac{1}{10}$, $F(k)=\dfrac{1024}{10}$), so $F(10)-F(0)=0$ is not the value of the integral.
Split $[0,10]$ into $[k,k+1]$, $k=0,\dots,9$. On $[k,k+1)$, $\{x\}=x-k$, and with $t=x-k$, each piece equals $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}(t-2)^{9}dt$.
This sum is evaluated by the continuous antiderivative on $[0,1]$: $\left[\dfrac{(t-2)^{10}}{10}\right]_{0}^{1}=\dfrac{(-1)^{10}-(-2)^{10}}{10}=\dfrac{1-1024}{10}=-102.3$.
originality_note: New: a binomial sum in the fractional part {x} collapses to ({x}-2)^9, whose obvious antiderivative is discontinuous at every integer, so the integral must be split and each unit piece is a C_r/(r+1)-type sum (way 5). Closest known: integral of a function of {x} over [0, n] by periodicity. Different because: the integrand is given as a binomial sum and the naive antiderivative gives 0.

concept_use.Binomial sums by the integration techniq: Each unit integral equals sum C(9,r)(-2)^(9-r)/(r+1), the integral over [0,1] of (t-2)^9.
concept_use.Evaluation via the antiderivative; handl: The antiderivative ({x}-2)^10/10 jumps at integers, so F(10) - F(0) = 0 is wrong and the interval is split.

stem_review: Read as a student: {t} defined, f has domain and codomain, the sum is finite; the answer does not depend on the value of f at integers; answer -1023 is a negative integer as planned; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: See f = ({x}-2)^9 and avoid the discontinuous antiderivative by working on unit intervals.
justification: Two linked ideas: recognising the binomial sum, and handling a periodic integrand whose antiderivative jumps; numerical. Comparable to 2024-P2-Q13 (L3, integral of a piecewise function), easier than 2021-P2-Q19 (L4).
